newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Toshiba to raise Philippine investment.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba to raise Philippine investment.

text.p: Japan's Toshiba Corp will spend an additional six billion yen on its Philippine plant to expand product lines, company president Taizo Nishimuro told reporters on Wednesday.
Toshiba has already invested six billion yen, or 1.6 billion pesos, to build a plant in the Philippines under its wholly-owned unit Toshiba Information Equipment (Philippines Inc).
The plant, in Laguna province, south of Manila, has been manufacturing CD-ROM drives, hard disk drives (HDDs) and motherboards since October last year.

Under the new plans, six billion yen would be invested in the plant to produce high-capacity digital video disc read-only memory (DVD-ROM) drives for personal computers, said Takeo Nagatomo, president of the Philippine unit.
Production of the DVD-ROM drives was expected to start in 1998 at a monthly capacity of 100,000 to 200,000 units, he said.
For the fiscal year starting this April, production capacity at the Philippine plant would reach 3.4 million 2.5 inch HDDs, 6.2 million optical disc drives and 360,000 motherboards, Nagatomo said.

"By 1998, we will expand those levels to four million HDDs, 6.4 million optical disc drives and 700,000 motherboards," he said. "By the year 2000, we expect our accumulated investment to double that of today, while the number of employees will triple."
Toshiba officials said they expected healthy market growth due to the growing corporate investment in computers, and the attractions of the Internet.

"In the fiscal year ending March 1997, our consolidated global sales are expected to reach 5.5 trillion yen," Nishimuro said. The company had net sales of 5.12 trillion yen in the fiscal year ending March 31, 1996.
"The global PC market is expected to grow from 59.5 million units in 1996 to 78 million units in 1998," said Tetsuya Mizoguchi, vice president of Toshiba Corp.
"And the world market for 2.5-inch hard disk drives, where we are in business, is expected to exceed 16 million units this year, and reach 18.5 million next year," Mizoguchi added.
